title: StepFinder: A Temporal Semantic Framework for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems

problem.claim: Failure attribution aims to identify the root-cause step responsible for failures in multi-agent systems.

gap.claim: Existing methods rely on LLM reasoning over original execution trajectories, incurring high inference cost and latency while noisy, redundant logs interfere with accurate root-cause identification.

contributions.claim: StepFinder is a lightweight failure-attribution framework that encodes execution logs into temporal semantic sequences using LLMs only during feature construction.
The framework combines parameter-efficient temporal modeling and attention modules to capture sequential evolution and cross-step dependencies.
It refines step-level error scores using multi-scale differences and position bias for root-cause identification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the Who&When benchmark, StepFinder reportedly outperforms LLM-based methods in step-level failure attribution.
StepFinder reportedly reduces inference time by 79% compared with the fastest LLM-based method.
The reported efficiency result involves no text-generation overhead, and code is reported as available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-agent systems support complex multi-step collaboration but are sensitive to execution errors that can cascade.
Failure attribution is introduced to identify the root-cause step of a failure.
Prior LLM-based approaches face cost, latency, and noisy-log interference.
StepFinder constructs temporal semantic features, models temporal and cross-step dependencies, and refines error scores.
The authors report benchmark gains and a 79% inference-time reduction relative to the fastest LLM-based method.

source_observation.claim: Redundant and noisy execution logs can interfere with LLM-based root-cause identification.

interpretation.claim: Failure attribution may benefit from structured representations that reduce reliance on raw trajectory text.

application.claim: For multi-step agent monitoring, consider converting logs into temporal semantic features before downstream attribution.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this approach is effective outside the reported benchmark or task setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark size, evaluation metrics, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not describe the temporal model, attention modules, or multi-scale difference and position-bias formulation in detail.
The abstract does not provide error-analysis results or independent verification.
